title: Charred Cabbage Caesar with Rye Crumbs and Capers
changes_from_base: Pan-charred cabbage wedges replace the raw romaine, with crisp rye crumbs and capers instead of ciabatta croutons.
summary: Green cabbage wedges charred in a hot pan until smoky and sweet, drizzled with a creamy anchovy Caesar dressing and scattered with crisp rye crumbs, capers and Parmesan.
equipment: large heavy (cast-iron) frying pan with lid

ingredients.item: small green cabbage (about 900 g), cut into 8 wedges through the core
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard, tamarind, anchovies, garlic and pepper together.

steps.title: Crisp the rye
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the pan over medium heat and fry the rye crumbs, stirring, for 6-8 min until crisp. Tip onto a plate.

steps.title: Char the cabbage
steps.text: Brush the wedges with 2 tbsp oil. Heat the rest of the oil in the pan over medium-high heat, add half the wedges cut side down, sprinkle with half the salt, cover and cook 3-4 min per side until deeply charred and just tender. Repeat.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Lay the wedges on the platter, scatter with capers, drizzle with half the dressing, then add the rye crumbs, Parmesan and more pepper. Serve the rest of the dressing alongside.

tips: A heavy cast-iron pan gives the deepest char.
Cut through the core so each wedge holds together.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
storage: Best on the day. Leftover wedges keep 1 day in the fridge; the dressing keeps 3 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
